newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan to auction 40 pct of telecom monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan to auction 40 pct of telecom monopoly.

text.p: Kazakhstan will hold a new tender for 40 percent of its Kazakhtelecom monopoly after a deal with Deutsche Telekom fell through, the Kazakh State Property Committee said on Monday.
A spokesman said that bids for the government stake would be accepted through February 21 but it did not name a starting price.
A committee press release said tender conditions required that the winner reinvest income from the stake for five years.
The winner must replace 550,000 old lines and bring installed line base to three million lines in five years and 4.2-4.5 million lines in 10 years.
It must also take on responsibility for $250 million in loans and interest owed by NK Kazakhtelekom by 2003.
A deal with Deutsche Telekom AG for 49 percent of the company fell through in December. A banker close to the deal said the German company had found the deal too costly.
Deutsche Telekom had agreeed to pay 825 million marks, including payments towards paying off company debt, for the stake, and promised to install 4.5 million lines within 10 years.

Birzhana Madiyev, head of the State Property Committee's privatisation department for key industries, said Kazakhstan decided to reduce the stake at offer to 40 percent as part of plans to sell part of the company on the stock market.
He gave no other details of the plan to sell shares on the market.
Kazakhtelekom has 19 regional units and owns a number of telephone-related industries in Kazakhstan. The government owns 90 percent of the company and workers own the remaining 10 percent.
